FY2026 quarterly figures are reported actuals for Q1-Q3; Q4 is management guidance.

findings.claim: FY2026 is running at exceptional growth: Q1 revenue USD 143.8bn (+16%), Q2 USD 111.2bn (+17%), Q3 USD 109.4bn (+16%). Nine-month revenue of USD 364.4bn against FY2025 full-year revenue of USD 416.2bn.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The driver is an iPhone replacement cycle, not a new category. iPhone revenue rose 22% in both the March quarter (USD 56.99bn) and the June quarter (USD 54.3bn). iPhone 17 outsold iPhone 16 by 14% in the first ten days in the US and China.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: FY2026 revenue is estimated at approximately USD 477bn (+14.7%), from nine months actual of USD 364.4bn plus a Q4 estimate of USD 113bn at the midpoint of the guided 9-11% growth on an estimated USD 102.8bn prior-year quarter.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: 364.4 + 102.8 x 1.10. Prior-year Q4 derived as 416.16 less the three implied year-ago quarters

findings.claim: FY2026 net income is estimated at approximately USD 131bn (+17%) and EPS at approximately USD 8.89, from nine-month actuals of USD 101.5bn and USD 6.87 respectively plus a fourth quarter at a guided 47-48% gross margin.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Q1-Q3 FY2026 reported net income and EPS plus Q4 guidance

findings.claim: Services reached USD 109.16bn in FY2025 at a 75.4% gross margin — the first year above USD 100bn — and is running at approximately USD 125bn in FY2026.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Apple FY2025 results; FY2026 quarterly releases

findings.claim: Services growth is decelerating while hardware accelerates — the reverse of the accepted narrative. Services grew 16% in Q2 FY2026 but 12% in Q3, and missed consensus of USD 31.22bn at USD 30.74bn. iPhone grew 22% in both quarters.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Apple Q2/Q3 FY2026 results; Yahoo Finance and Quartz, 2026-07-30

findings.claim: The installed base exceeds 2.5 billion active devices, up 150 million year on year, with more than 1.5 billion paid subscriptions. This is the annuity that underwrites Services.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Apple Q1 FY2026 release, 2026-01-29; Q3 FY2026

findings.claim: Roughly 16% of Services revenue is the Google default-search payment (USD 20bn of approximately USD 125bn), carrying a materially higher share of Services profit given its near-zero cost. Services growth and Services quality are therefore not the same question.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Demand classification: the iPhone 17 cycle and the installed base are [Existing Contracted] in substance — recurring, evidenced, already in the run rate. The Gemini-powered Siri launching with iOS 27 in September 2026 is [Approved / Committed Pipeline]. A Siri-driven upgrade supercycle is [Speculative Demand] and belongs only in the bull case.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Applying the Phase 3 classification test to the demand evidence

findings.claim: Apple unveiled the rebuilt Siri on 8 June 2026, routing its hardest reasoning to Google's Gemini models, with full conversational Siri shipping in iOS 27 in September 2026 — roughly two years after the capability was first demonstrated in 2024.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Incremental margin is currently above average margin — the rare case where growth is accretive rather than dilutive. Q3 FY2026 net income grew 27% (USD 23.43bn to USD 29.79bn) on 16% revenue growth. Approximately 2pp of the gross margin was a non-recurring tariff refund.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Q3 FY2026 reported figures

gaps.whyItMatters: ~16% of Services revenue and considerably more of its profit is one contract now repriced annually. Services growth ex-Google is the number that matters and it is not disclosed.
gaps.resolvedBy: Apple does not break this out; it would have to be estimated from Google's own filings

gaps.item: Whether the iPhone 17 cycle pulls demand forward
gaps.whyItMatters: Two quarters at +22% against a normal replacement cadence raises the question of whether FY2027 faces an air pocket. The Q4 guidance of +9-11% is already a deceleration.

gaps.item: Why Services decelerated to +12% and missed consensus
gaps.whyItMatters: Services is the high-margin annuity underwriting the multiple. A deceleration there is worth more than an acceleration in hardware.

risks.text: Services decelerated to +12% and missed consensus in Q3 FY2026 while the market continues to value Apple on the Services annuity story.
The FY2026 growth surge is a replacement cycle, not a new category. Replacement cycles pull demand forward and end; Q4 guidance already decelerates to +9-11%.
The Siri supercycle thesis is unevidenced. Full conversational Siri ships two years late and on a competitor's model.

catalysts.text: iOS 27 with full conversational Siri ships
Q1 FY2027 results — first read on whether the iPhone 17 cycle pulled demand forward

conclusions: FY2026 is an outstanding year: approximately USD 477bn of revenue (+14.7%) and USD 131bn of net income (+17%), driven by an iPhone 17 replacement cycle running at +22% for two consecutive quarters.
Growth is currently accretive — incremental margin exceeds average margin, and net income grew 27% on 16% revenue in Q3. This is the opposite of the volume-without-value trap.

But the composition is the wrong way round for the story the market is paying for. Services, the high-margin annuity that justifies the multiple, decelerated from +16% to +12% and missed consensus; hardware, the cyclical line, is carrying the growth.
Roughly 16% of Services revenue, and considerably more of its profit, is a single contract with Google that a court has just converted to a 12-month non-exclusive arrangement.
Applying the classification discipline: the supercycle that much of the bullish case depends on is [Speculative Demand] and earns zero weight in a base case.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 sharpens the question for Phase 5. Apple is not expensive because it is not growing — it is growing strongly and profitably. It is expensive because the market is capitalising a cyclical hardware surge and a decelerating Services line at a multiple that assumes both are permanent. The valuation work has to test what growth rate the price actually embeds.
